method: District metrics = features within 25 km of each district anchor, computed from the six map layers (MRDS, state surveys, USMIN workings, BLM active/filed/closed claims), snapshot 2026-07-30. "Filed" = claims BLM has not finished adjudicating — the freshest staking signal available since location dates are not in the public GIS. News verified against primary sources July 2026; two items marked partial in news_2026.json.

top10.title: Stibnite is actually being built
top10.why: After 8 years of permitting, Perpetua's Stibnite gold-antimony mine broke ground in Oct 2025, closed a $2.9B EXIM loan in May 2026, survived an injunction attempt days later, and is building the Burntlog access road now — first US mined antimony since 1997, targeted 2029. The data agrees it's the epicenter: 3,070 active claims within 25 km (the largest cluster in the entire Northwest), 709 of them newly filed.

top10.title: Silver Valley's full-blown revival
top10.why: Bunker Hill poured its first concentrate in 45 years on June 29, 2026; Lucky Friday just set an all-time record (5.3 Moz silver in 2025); Galena is expanding its mill 750→1,200 tpd by year-end. The Coeur d'Alene district shows the densest convergence in the dataset: 1,772 mapped historic workings, 2,208 active claims, 736 freshly filed — every layer lights up at once.

top10.title: The Idaho staking rush
top10.why: 46% of Idaho's 40,624 active claims — 18,856 of them — are in FILED (pending) status, meaning they were located so recently BLM hasn't finished adjudicating them. No other state is close (WY 30%, OR 20%, MT 1%). Gold at record prices plus the critical-minerals push is re-staking Idaho at a pace the other four states combined can't match.

top10.title: Black Pine — the mine growing in Cody's backyard
top10.why: Liberty Gold's 3.11 Moz oxide project in Cassia County entered federal EIS scoping April 3, 2026 under FAST-41, with a feasibility study due Q4 2026 and first gold targeted 2028. The claim wall is visible from orbit: the districts around it are absorbing the staking spillover — the four Cassia deep-dive districts each show 410–460 newly filed claims within 25 km.

top10.title: Wyoming uranium is back on
top10.why: Shirley Basin started operations April 2026, Lost Creek captured 110,314 lb in Q1, UEC's Christensen Ranch keeps ramping — US Q1 2026 uranium output was the best first quarter since 2015. It shows in the ground game: Wyoming's 40,873 active claims essentially tie Idaho for most in the region, with 12,123 pending filings concentrated in the uranium and REE belts.

top10.title: Rare earths arrive via a coal mine
top10.why: Ramaco's Brook Mine near Sheridan — opened July 2025 as Wyoming's first new coal mine in ~50 years — exists mostly for what's IN the coal: rare earths. The pilot oxide plant comes online in 2026 and a July 25, 2026 expansion targets ~3,400 t/yr of oxides. Across the border, US Critical Materials' Sheep Creek (MT) carries the region's other REE hopes on a FAST-41 listing — though still no drilling, a gap worth watching skeptically.

top10.title: The antimony scramble
top10.why: China's late-2024 export ban sent antimony above $60/kg (it's ~$52 now, still triple the old normal). US Antimony's Thompson Falls smelter landed a $245M five-year Defense Logistics Agency stockpile contract, commissioned a new smelter in Q2 2026, and is reopening Montana antimony mining at Stibnite Hill — while Perpetua's Stibnite (#1) carries the long-term supply answer.

top10.title: South Pass: the quiet gold rush nobody is reporting
top10.why: Wyoming's 1867 gold district shows 960 newly FILED claims within 25 km — the single largest fresh-staking signal of any district in the five states, bigger than Stibnite's or the Silver Valley's. There is no matching news flow: this one is visible only in the claims data. Somebody believes in South Pass at current gold prices.

top10.title: Oregon wakes up: first gold ROD + a giant lithium number
top10.why: Grassy Mountain got its BLM Record of Decision on Jan 29, 2026 — the first modern gold mine ever federally approved in Oregon ($375M NPV at the feasibility study's $3,600/oz price deck; state permits still pending). And Jindalee's McDermitt project holds 21.5 Mt LCE, the largest US lithium resource, heading for a Nasdaq listing late 2026. Oregon's 2,234 pending claim filings say the ground game has started.

top10.title: Orphan ground — where the old-timers dug but nobody holds claims
top10.why: The inverse signal: districts dense with mapped historic workings but nearly empty of active claims. Canyon Creek, OR is the standout — 221 topo-map workings, 1,564 once-staked-now-closed claims, and only 40 active ones today. The Stokes district in Cassia County (44 active claims over 40 workings) is the same story in Cody's county. Open ground with proven digging history is exactly what a prospector's map is for — verify withdrawal status and land ownership first.

news.topic: Perpetua Resources' Stibnite Gold Project, Valley County ID (gold + antimony)
news.status_2026: Early-works construction began in October 2025 (following the January 2025 ROD), and the 2026 field season is underway: Burntlog Route access-road construction commenced May 30, 2026, alongside worker housing, powerline upgrades and geotechnical drilling, with ~$45 million of direct 2026 work for Idaho contractors; a U.S. District Court denied a preliminary injunction against the project on May 29, 2026. On May 21, 2026 the Export-Import Bank of the United States approved a $2.9 billion, 13-year senior secured loan (upfront facility of $2.4 billion, priced at long-dated Treasuries +100 bp, repayments from 2030), with definitive documentation/financial close expected in H2 2026. Perpetua is targeting operations in 2029, including delivery of antimony to the U.S. military by 2029; Stibnite holds the only identified domestic antimony reserve (company says it could meet ~35% of U.S. antimony demand in early production years). Federal defense support to date totals ~$59.4M under DPA Title III ($24.8M Dec 2022 + $34.6M Feb 2024) plus up to $6.9M awarded in May 2025 for a domestic antimony-trisulfide supply chain.

news.topic: Bunker Hill Mine restart, Kellogg ID (Silver Valley) — zinc-lead-silver
news.status_2026: Yes — the restart hit its H1 2026 target: on June 29, 2026 Bunker Hill announced production of first concentrate, the first product shipped from the mine in 45 years, with concentrate going to Teck's Trail smelter in B.C. The processing plant is rated 1,800 tonnes per day with a future expansion path to 2,500 tpd. Commercial production (defined as 90 days at >65% of 1,800 tpd with operating stability) is expected by end of 2026, at which point the company will issue 2027-28 operating guidance. A March 16, 2026 update had confirmed the project was on track for the June 2026 restart.

news.topic: Hecla's Lucky Friday mine, Mullan ID; Galena Complex (Americas Gold & Silver)
news.status_2026: Lucky Friday set annual records in 2025: 5.3 Moz silver (+8% YoY) on record mill throughput averaging 1,170 tons/day; Hecla's companywide 2025 silver output was 17.0 Moz (announced Jan 26, 2026). Hecla's 2026 Lucky Friday guidance is 4.7-5.2 Moz silver with $68-73M of capital including a new tailings facility and a surface cooling project due for completion by mid-2026. At the Galena Complex, Americas Gold & Silver's April 27, 2026 update detailed the No. 3 Shaft hoist upgrade (Phase 1 complete with a new 2,250-hp motor; ~150% hoisting-rate increase toward 1,350 stpd capacity), a mill expansion from 750 to 1,200 stpd targeted by end-2026, and a paste backfill plant commissioning in Q4 2026, with ~650 stpd average ore hoisting planned for the balance of 2026; the nearby Crescent mine (acquired December 2025) has had key systems restored with 2,000 ft of development planned in Q2 2026.

news.topic: Sibanye-Stillwater's Stillwater & East Boulder PGM mines, MT
news.status_2026: Both Montana operations continue mining, but the Stillwater West section remains on care and maintenance following the late-2024 restructuring that cut ~700 jobs (~40% of the workforce); the US PGM business returned to profitability in H2 2025, helped by Section 45X production credits (~$285M recognized through H1 2025) and recovering palladium prices, and Sibanye is targeting AISC of ~$1,000/2E oz within 2-3 years (2E reserves were 19.4 Moz at end-2025). In the trade case Sibanye brought, the Commerce Department's International Trade Administration issued a preliminary antidumping determination (reported Feb 20, 2026) imposing a preliminary 132% duty on Russian palladium, with the countervailing/subsidy portion still pending; palladium traded around $1,600-1,795/oz in February 2026 versus $800-1,000 during the dumping period. Q1 2026 production was 5% lower YoY with AISC up 14%, and no restart date for Stillwater West has been announced; the Stillwater mine expansion was added to the FAST-41 transparency list in May 2025.

news.topic: United States Antimony Corp (UAMY), Thompson Falls MT smelter
news.status_2026: USAC won a $245 million, five-year sole-source Defense Logistics Agency contract (announced early October 2025) to supply antimony ingots for the National Defense Stockpile, and in Q2 2026 delivered its first two shipments (~82,000 lb, ~$2.6M invoiced in June 2026) while commissioning expanded smelting furnaces at a newly constructed Thompson Falls facility; a ~$20M expansion targets ~400 tons/month of capacity (~5x prior levels) and ~25 new jobs (MTPR, Apr 6, 2026). On sourcing, USAC is reactivating mining at Stibnite Hill adjacent to the smelter (Small Miner Exclusion Statement filed July 2025; surface mining reported underway by April 2026) and has built a large Alaska claims position (144 claims/~8,998 acres in the Fairbanks area as of Apr 7, 2025, and 35,000+ total Alaska acres per its July 2025 release, plus Stibnite Creek and Maclaren River claims). Antimony prices have cooled from post-China-export-ban records: ~$51.8/kg in late July 2026, down ~45% from the ~$94.85/kg peak roughly a year earlier.

news.topic: US Critical Materials' Sheep Creek REE-gallium project, Ravalli County MT
news.status_2026: Sheep Creek was added to the FAST-41 transparency list on Nov 19, 2025 (with USFS as lead agency; the listing describes gallium plus neodymium/praseodymium/niobium targets spanning southwest Montana and east-central Idaho), and on April 9, 2026 the company announced receipt of a USGS technical report from a 45,506 line-km airborne magnetic/radiometric survey flown Oct 2023-Sep 2024. However, as of late November 2025 local reporting found no exploration drilling had ever occurred (surface sampling only) and no Plan of Operations had been submitted to the Bitterroot National Forest; the company's own 2025-26 strategy emphasizes pilot beneficiation and an INL Phase II CRADA on REE/gallium separation, with production still years away. No 2025-26 DoD or DOE funding award could be verified — the company states it is seeking DOD/DOE funding; its high-grade claims remain based on surface samples, and local watershed-focused opposition is active.

news.topic: Ramaco Resources' Brook Mine, Sheridan County WY (coal + rare earths)
news.status_2026: The Brook Mine opened with a ribbon-cutting on July 11, 2025 — billed as the first new U.S. rare earth mine in ~70 years and Wyoming's first new coal mine in ~50 years — and Ramaco broke ground on its pilot processing plant and lab adjacent to the mine on Oct 23, 2025, supported by a $6.1M Wyoming Energy Authority matching grant. On July 25, 2026 Ramaco announced an accelerated expansion: target oxide output raised to ~3,400 tons/year of REE/critical-mineral oxides (from 1,240), coal production rising from 2 to 5 Mtpa (permit area expanding from 4,500 to ~16,000 acres), the pilot plant to begin operating later in 2026, and construction of a full-scale commercial oxide plant targeted to start in 2026 (18-month build), backed by a $200M equity raise and a credit facility upsized to $400M. Note that Ramaco's rare-earth grade and economics claims drew public scrutiny from some geologists and short-sellers in late 2025 (Cowboy State Daily, Nov 16, 2025).

news.topic: Wyoming uranium ISR restarts: Ur-Energy (Lost Creek, Shirley Basin), UEC (Irigaray/Christensen Ranch), Cameco (Smith Ranch-Highland)
news.status_2026: Ur-Energy's Lost Creek captured 110,314 lb U3O8 in Q1 2026 (+41% vs Q4 2025), shipping 103,956 lb, with Q1 revenue of $3.9M on 55,000 lb sold at $70.98/lb; Shirley Basin — Wyoming's first new-build ISR mine in decades — commenced operations in April 2026 with uranium loading onto resin, first resin shipments to Lost Creek expected in summer 2026 after final WDEQ transport authorization, and construction continuing into 2027. UEC's Christensen Ranch/Irigaray (Willow Creek) operation, restarted in August 2024, had produced ~277,000 lb cumulatively through April 30, 2026 (32,195 lb in fiscal Q3 FY2026) with new Wellfield 11 header houses coming online and five more under construction. Cameco's Smith Ranch-Highland officially remains curtailed (suspended since 2016; 2026 care-and-maintenance cost guidance US$14-15M), although EIA counts it among six U.S. facilities recording some Q1 2026 output (see cameco.com); total U.S. Q1 2026 production was 1,039,075 lb U3O8, the highest first quarter since 2015.

news.topic: Wyoming trona/soda ash, Green River basin — expansions and 2025-26 market
news.status_2026: WE Soda completed its $1.43 billion acquisition of Genesis Alkali's Green River operations in February 2025, becoming the world's largest soda ash producer; it trimmed 26 non-union positions in June 2025 while targeting growth to over 11 Mt/year by 2030, and in March 2026 the USW local secured an $800,000 overtime settlement. Pacific Soda's Dry Creek project won BLM approval in May 2025 (planned ~6 Mt/year of soda ash, up to 2,000 construction jobs and ~300 permanent). The market remains difficult: ChemAnalyst reported (May 28, 2026) that persistent global oversupply and discounted imports kept U.S. soda ash prices soft into mid-2026, with only a weak recovery outlook. No 2025-26 Sisecam Wyoming expansion decision could be verified — its previously announced Wyoming expansion ambitions predate 2025 and no newer confirmation was found.

news.topic: Paramount Gold Nevada's Grassy Mountain gold project, Malheur County OR
news.status_2026: Paramount announced on January 29, 2026 that BLM signed the Record of Decision approving Grassy Mountain following the Final EIS — federal approval for what would be Oregon's first modern gold mine. Oregon state permits (the DOGAMI-coordinated consolidated permitting process) were still pending as of Feb 3, 2026 reporting, and no construction start date has been announced, though the company calls the project shovel-ready. An updated feasibility study announced May 28, 2026 showed an after-tax NPV of $375M and 39% IRR at $3,600/oz gold.

news.topic: Jindalee Lithium's McDermitt project, Malheur County OR (McDermitt caldera)
news.status_2026: Jindalee's McDermitt project at the northern (Oregon) end of the McDermitt caldera hosts a 2025-updated mineral resource of 21.5 Mt of lithium carbonate equivalent — the largest lithium deposit in the U.S. by contained LCE — and a late-2024 pre-feasibility study outlined a mine life exceeding 60 years using only part of the resource. The McDermitt Exploration Project was among the first ten FAST-41 transparency projects announced April 18, 2025. In 2026 Jindalee is spinning its U.S. assets into 'US Elemental' via a SPAC merger targeting a Nasdaq listing in Q3-Q4 2026 (Jindalee retaining ~80%), with H2 2026 infill drilling and the start of a feasibility study targeted for completion by end-2027 and federal permits by end-2028.

news.topic: Hecla's Montanore (Libby Exploration Project) and Rock Creek copper-silver projects, Libby MT area
news.status_2026: The U.S. Forest Service approved Hecla's Libby Exploration Project — the reconfigured evaluation phase of the Montanore copper-silver project — in October 2025, and on July 9, 2026 the Federal Permitting Council announced the project had completed federal permitting (the 19th mining project to do so under the current administration; it was a FAST-41 transparency project). The plan is to dewater the existing adit and extend it 4,200 ft plus ~6,300 ft of new tunnels for a multi-year underground evaluation (about 16 years including reclamation, employing 30-35). Six conservation groups represented by Earthjustice sued over the approval in federal court in Missoula on about April 1, 2026, citing grizzly bear, bull trout and Cabinet Mountains Wilderness water impacts. Rock Creek (Sanders County) remains on hold — Hecla has said it will not pursue exploration permits there until Libby/Montanore advances.

news.topic: Kinross Buckhorn/Kettle River WA legacy, Crown Resources water litigation; WA metal mining in 2026
news.status_2026: The Okanogan Highlands Alliance's Clean Water Act citizen suit settled on November 1, 2024: Crown Resources/Kinross will fund $3 million in upper-Columbia conservation projects and undertake pollutant-source investigations and a corrective action plan, after a 2022 federal ruling found 3,000+ permit violations (Crown acknowledged 3,500+ monthly violations, over 100,000 violation-days, Feb 2015-Jul 2022); Washington State's parallel case was not part of that settlement and was still ongoing at the time — no 2025-26 resolution of the state case could be verified. Reverse-osmosis water treatment at the closed mine has run since 2014 and long-term treatment/monitoring obligations continue. Buckhorn operated 2008-2017 and was Washington's last producing gold mine; no operating metal mine in Washington in 2026 could be identified (WA DNR's mining page was inaccessible for direct confirmation, and no restart announcements were found).

news.topic: Federal critical-minerals push relevant to the NW: FAST-41 projects, executive actions, DPA/defense funding
news.status_2026: FAST-41 now covers a large NW slate: Stibnite (covered project; ROD Jan 2025, $2.9B EXIM loan approved May 21, 2026) and Black Pine (covered project; NOI Apr 3, 2026), plus transparency-list projects including Stillwater Mine expansion (added May 2025), UEC's Sweetwater uranium project WY (Aug 1, 2025), Blue Copper MT (Aug 22, 2025), Sheep Creek MT/ID (Nov 19, 2025), and Resolution Minerals' Golden Gate tungsten-gold project near Yellow Pine ID (Jul 17, 2026); Antimony Ridge (Resolution Minerals, ID), DeLamar (ID) and Grassy Mountain (OR) also appear on the current transparency list, McDermitt Exploration (OR) was in the initial ten announced Apr 18, 2025, and Hecla's Libby Exploration Project completed federal permitting Jul 9, 2026. Defense/DPA money touching NW mines: Perpetua has received ~$59.4M under DPA Title III ($24.8M Dec 2022 + $34.6M Feb 2024) plus up to $6.9M (May 2025) for the antimony-trisulfide supply chain; USAC holds a $245M five-year DLA stockpile contract (Oct 2025) with first deliveries in Q2 2026; Sibanye-Stillwater's Montana PGM operations benefit from Section 45X credits (~$285M recognized through H1 2025) and preliminary 132% antidumping duties on Russian palladium (Feb 2026). These flow from the administration's 2025 critical-minerals permitting push (March 2025 minerals executive order and subsequent Permitting Council actions).
